subject: Benchmark playbook confirmation + streaming specs
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@novaretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-10T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap & ask: latency SLOs, streaming behavior, and next steps

Hi Evan — great call today, thanks for walking us through your production constraints. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

- Target SLOs you mentioned: p95 end-to-end latency <= 150ms for typical 256-token completions; p99 <= 300ms for business-critical queries.
- Concurrency target: sustained 50 concurrent sessions during peak (checkout window), bursts to 150 for short periods.
- Streaming requirement: partial-token delivery for UX; target chunk emission interval <= 80ms from Redwood runtime to client when streaming small responses.
- Throughput estimate: ~220 rps overall, with a heavy tail of short (30–50 token) completions.

Requests: 
1) Can you confirm whether end-to-end latency measurement should include your frontend websocket hop (yes/no)? If yes, we will instrument and report end-to-end numbers; otherwise we'll provide model+runtime-only breakdowns.
2) Please upload one representative prompt bundle (sample sizes: 200 long, 600 short) and any synthetic concurrency workload you prefer. You can drop it in the shared Drive.

We will:
- Draft a compact benchmark playbook (measurement definitions, warm-up, sampling, reproducibility checks).
- Provide an eval harness (Docker + run script) that runs with the prompt bundle you share, produces p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail histograms, and streaming chunk timing.

Attaching a first-pass prompt bundle (nr_prompt_set_v2.jsonl) and a short playbook draft. Marcus will take lead on the harness.

Next steps: you confirm measurement scope and share any internal load generator config by Monday 9/13; we aim to have a reproducible run and initial readout by 9/14.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | https://redwood.ai

Attachments: nr_prompt_set_v2.jsonl (sample prompts), redwood-benchmark-playbook-v1.md (draft)

From: Evan Park <evan.park@novaretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: perf-team@novaretail.com
Date: 2027-09-11T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap & ask: latency SLOs, streaming behavior, and next steps

Jordan — thanks for the concise recap. Quick answers and clarifications: 

- End-to-end measurement: include the frontend websocket hop. We want to validate the user-visible 95th percentiles. We will provide a lightweight agent for measurement if that helps (we have a small telemetry script).
- Prompt bundle: uploaded to your Drive folder at /NovaRetail/samples/v2 (200 long, 600 short) and included a small synthetic load config (k6 script) for concurrency shaping.
- Streaming: critical for our checkout UX. Chunk interval target <= 75ms if possible; if not, we need clear degradation behavior (e.g., fall back to non-streaming or batched chunks).

On scope: please include TLS handshake and our proxy (we run through an internal edge) in the end-to-end measurement. If you include those hops we can validate the entire path.

We also want to capture KV cache hit vs cold-start cases for repeated prompts (20% cacheable pattern expected).

I'll schedule a 30-min sync on Tuesday to review the playbook after your updates.

—Evan
Principal Product Manager, NovaRetail
perf-team@novaretail.com

Attachment: nova_perf_trace_sample.txt (sample trace)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: draft harness notes + measurement clarifications

Quick internal notes after Evan's confirmation: 

- Measurement definition: end-to-end = client send -> client receive final token (includes websocket/proxy/TLS). We'll capture: model_compute_ms, runtime_ms, network_ms (edge), total_e2e_ms.
- Warmup: 3000 tokens or 5 minutes of ramp per run to populate KV cache and JIT paths.
- Sampling: runs of 10k short prompts and 3k long prompts per config (to get stable p99).
- Concurrency shaping: use NovaRetail k6 script but gate at client-side time to avoid synthetic queueing in their proxy. We'll run both 'native concurrency' (real clients) and 'synthetic concurrency' via our harness to isolate runtime behavior.
- Streaming checks: instrument chunk arrival timestamps at both client and runtime side. We will compute chunk_interval_ms distribution and percentiles. Fail criteria: median chunk_interval > 120ms or p95 > 220ms for streaming mode flagged as degraded.

I'll build a Docker-based harness that accepts: prompt bundle, concurrency profile, quant settings (int8/float16), and streaming flag. Output: CSV of latencies, chunk intervals, and a reproducibility hash (run-seed + docker image sha).

Grace — can you add the reproducibility checklist to the playbook: docker sha, model config, seed, randomization knobs, measurement timestamp, and host kernel version. I'll link our initial harness in the Drive when ready.

- Marcus
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Sep 12, 2027, at 10:37 AM, Marcus Lin wrote:
> Quick internal notes after Evan's confirmation...

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@novaretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Revised playbook + harness link — please review before Tuesday sync

Evan — pushed an updated playbook that incorporates Marcus' checklist and your measurement scope. Changes in this version: 

- Explicit end-to-end measurement path (client websocket -> edge proxy -> runtime -> model -> back to client).
- Warm-up and sampling sizes per Marcus' note.
- Streaming acceptance criteria tightened to median chunk_interval <= 80ms and p95 <= 200ms.
- KV cache experiment plan: cold, warm, and warm-with-cold-injection (simulate 20% cacheable pattern).
- Run reproducibility: harness emits a run manifest.json and a run sha; we will store artifacts in your Drive folder under /NovaRetail/benchmarks/run-YYYYMMDD.

Link to harness & artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nova-playbooks (redwood-benchmark-harness: redwood/harness:sha256:abcd1234)

Attached to this email: redwood-benchmark-playbook-v1.md (updated), nr_prompt_set_v2.jsonl (copied), quick-qa.md (answers to expected questions).

Proposed Tuesday sync agenda (30m):
- 5m: confirm measurement scope and any proxy caveats
- 10m: review prompt bundle and sampling plan
- 10m: pick 2 configs to run first (float16 + int8 quant)
- 5m: confirm timeline for artifact delivery (readout by Wed 9/15)

If that works, Marcus will kick off the first reproducible run right after the meeting.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-playbook-v1.md, quick-qa.md

From: Evan Park <evan.park@novaretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: perf-team@novaretail.com
Date: 2027-09-14T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Revised playbook + harness link — please review before Tuesday sync

Jordan / Marcus — reviewed the updated playbook. A few quick confirmation points before the sync: 

1) TLS + proxy in scope — confirmed. We'll provide a short-lived test cert for the run.
2) KV cache plan — good. Please include a breakdown in the readout showing cold vs warm p95.
3) Streaming thresholds look reasonable; minor ask: add a lightweight client-side jitter of 5–10ms in the harness to simulate front-end processing.

We are green to proceed with the Tuesday 30-min slot. Marcus — please share the first-run manifest plus a small CSV preview ahead of the call so our perf team can triage quickly.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the reproducible runs.

—Evan
Principal Product Manager, NovaRetail

Forwarded attachment: link to /NovaRetail/benchmarks/run-20270914/manifest.json (will appear after run)
